stem.text: A curve is defined by \( 4\left(y - 3\right)^{2} = \left(x\right)^{2}\left(x + 48\right) \), and its derivative is \( \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\left(x\right)\left(3x + 96\right)}{8\left(y - 3\right)} \). Find every point of the curve at which the tangent line is horizontal, or show that there is none.

answer_key.label: The tangent line is horizontal at \( (-32, 67) \) and \( (-32, -61) \).

worked_solution.text: A horizontal tangent needs the numerator of dy/dx to be 0 and the denominator to be nonzero. The numerator is 0 when \( x = 0 \) or \( x = -32 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: numerator of dy/dx equal to zero

worked_solution.text: On the curve, \( x = 0 \) forces \( y = 3 \), where the denominator is also 0, so \( (0, 3) \) is not a point with a horizontal tangent.
Substituting \( x = -32 \) into the curve gives \( \left(y - 3\right)^{2} = 4096 \), so \( y = 67 \) or \( y = -61 \), and the denominator is nonzero at both points.

options.label: The tangent line is horizontal at \( (0, 3) \) and \( (-32, 3) \).
options.derivation: the numerator's roots paired with y = 3 and reported without substituting into the curve

options.label: The tangent line is horizontal at \( (-32, 67) \) and \( (-32, -61) \).
The tangent line is horizontal at \( (0, 3) \), \( (-32, 67) \) and \( (-32, -61) \).
options.derivation: the point (0, 3), where the numerator is 0, kept without checking that the denominator is also 0 there

options.label: The tangent line is horizontal at \( (0, 3) \) and \( (-48, 3) \).
options.derivation: the denominator set to 0 instead of the numerator, which finds the points where y = v
